messages:
Kenji Nakamura: Dropping latest Rollout Wizard flow for UX review. Main open questions are guardrail defaults + confirmation dialogs (trying to reduce risk of misconfig). Figma: https://figma.com/file/RdwD-HostedRollouts/Canary-Wizard?node-id=214-880

Kenji Nakamura: Specifically:
1) Do we default guardrails ON w/ recommended thresholds?
2) When do we require confirmations? (e.g. setting Candidate to 100%, removing guardrails, enabling timed progression)
3) Copy/tone for “you are about to send X% traffic to Candidate”

Svetlana Orlov: :eyes: taking a look now

Marissa Cole: thanks Kenji. +1 on making it hard to shoot yourself in the foot. We had that beta incident where someone accidentally pushed 100% w/ no rollback plan.

Dylan Brooks: Looking. From implementation POV, confirm dialogs are easy; enforcing “guardrails required” depends on the validation rules we land in control plane. But UX can assume we’ll block w/ a clear error state.

Svetlana Orlov: First pass feedback:
- The stepper is good.
- Guardrails section: default toggles ON is consistent w/ our “safe by default” principle.
- But don’t pre-fill scary numbers w/o explanation. We should label as “Recommended defaults” and allow edit.

Svetlana Orlov: Also, for confirmation dialogs, our DS pattern is: only interrupt on irreversible/risky actions. Here: “Start rollout” (if it immediately impacts prod traffic), “Increase traffic”, “Remove all guardrails”, “Rollback”.

Kenji Nakamura: Helpful. In this flow, “Create rollout” saves as Draft (0% candidate) unless they explicitly Start. So impact only begins at Start.

Hannah Rivera: On pause/rollback flows we’ve been using “Pause is reversible, rollback is not” framing. For wizard: I’d avoid a confirmation every time they change % in the editor, but do confirm on Start + any schedule step that moves beyond a threshold.

Jada Williams: +1. If someone adds timed progression (e.g. 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% automatically) that’s the biggest footgun. We should force an explicit acknowledgment and require guardrails.

Paula Mendes: Agree. Also we should nudge them to add at least error-rate + latency guardrails by default. Cost delta is nice, but it’s more “budget control” than “safety”.

Kenji Nakamura: Proposed default set right now:
- Error rate delta: +0.5% absolute over baseline (5m window)
- p95 latency delta: +15% over baseline (5m)
- Token cost delta: +20% over baseline (15m)
Thoughts?

Marissa Cole: Those seem reasonable as a starting point but we need to avoid implying they’re universal. Can we present as presets: Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive?

Svetlana Orlov: Presets would be great. DS-wise, we can do a segmented control or dropdown. But keep it simple: “Recommended (Balanced)” selected by default + “Customize”.

Dylan Brooks: Presets are fine in UI, but pls ensure what we send to backend is explicit values, not “preset=balanced”. Otherwise audit diff is messy.

Kenji Nakamura: yep, UI can expand to actual numbers before submit.

Jada Williams: One nuance: what happens if baseline has near-zero traffic (new route) so deltas are meaningless? We should have UI messaging for “insufficient baseline data” and default to absolute thresholds instead.

Paula Mendes: Good call. Telemetry will often have low sample at start. Maybe guardrails should support: “candidate error rate > X%” OR “delta > Y”. If we only have delta, it might never trigger.

Dylan Brooks: Backend policy supports both modes in v2 (I think Ethan/Jordan are adding). If not, we can do “delta” but show “Needs baseline traffic” warning.

Kenji Nakamura: I’ll add a warning state in the guardrails step: “Some guardrails require baseline metrics; if unavailable, rollout may not auto-pause.”

Hannah Rivera: Confirmation dialog copy suggestion for timed progression:
Title: “You’re enabling automatic traffic increases”
Body: “Traffic will increase even if you are not online. Guardrails can pause the rollout automatically.”
Primary CTA: “Enable timed progression”
Secondary: “Cancel”

Svetlana Orlov: +1, and include a small “Review guardrails” link inside dialog that jumps back to that step (non-blocking).

Marissa Cole: Also: if they set candidate to 100% in the stepper, we should require them to type the route name or “100” (like destructive confirmations). That’s standard for high-risk.

Dylan Brooks: Typing confirmations are doable but slightly annoying. Another option: require an explicit checkbox: “I understand this will send all traffic to Candidate” + “I have verified Candidate health dashboards”.

Kenji Nakamura: I’m leaning checkbox + summary of guardrails applied. Typing route name feels heavy for a wizard that’s meant to be fast.

Svetlana Orlov: Checkbox is consistent w/ our other “deploy” patterns. Typing is usually for deletes.

Jada Williams: Can we gate 100% behind at least one guardrail OR a manual step (no timed progression)? Basically don’t allow “auto to 100%” without guardrails.

Paula Mendes: Yes pls. We should also block “Remove all guardrails” if schedule has any future auto steps. Otherwise it’s truly uncontrolled.

Dylan Brooks: From UX, if backend rejects, we should show inline error at the schedule editor: “Timed progression requires at least one enabled guardrail.”

Kenji Nakamura: Noted. I’ll update the spec:
- Default guardrails ON (Recommended/Balanced preset)
- Confirmations:
  a) Start rollout
  b) Enable timed progression
  c) Increase traffic beyond 50% (optional?)
  d) Set to 100% candidate
  e) Disable/remove all guardrails
- Validation messaging: timed progression requires >=1 guardrail; 100% requires explicit ack

Marissa Cole: For (c) I’d prefer confirm when crossing 50% AND when crossing 90%? But maybe that’s too much. Maybe just 100%.

Hannah Rivera: I’d do confirm for 100% only. For 50% we can show a non-modal “high traffic” banner in the summary.

Svetlana Orlov: Agree. Too many confirms = people click through.

Kenji Nakamura: Cool. I’ll implement “High impact change” banner at >50% in review step (non-blocking).

Dylan Brooks: One more: Preview Effective Routing screen—can we add a small callout like “Sticky routing: on/off” so customers understand session behavior? Seen confusion in beta.

Kenji Nakamura: Good idea. I’ll add it in the Preview step + in the final Review summary.

Paula Mendes: pls also include “Guardrails evaluate every N minutes” detail somewhere. Otherwise users expect instant pause.

Kenji Nakamura: Yep, will add “Evaluation cadence” line under each guardrail + in summary.

Svetlana Orlov: :thumbsup: once updated, tag me and I’ll do a quick DS pass for dialog/banners.

Kenji Nakamura: Will do. Thanks all.
